newsitem.title: UK: Copper to come under pressure by end'97 - Wolff.
newsitem.headline: Copper to come under pressure by end'97 - Wolff.

text.p: Copper prices will remain vulnerable to further upside spikes in coming months due to strong underlying demand and low commercial stocks but the market will be under pressure in the latter part of the year, metals trader Rudolf Wolff and Co said.

In a special copper market report, the London Metal Exchange (LME) trader said that increased selling pressure will stem from a prolonged period of rising exchange stocks, signifying the emergence of the much-reported supply surplus.
"We feel that copper has the potential to rally and target $2,715 in the third quarter before falling back below $2,000 in the longer term," Wolff analyst Martin Squires said in the report.
Copper production in 1997 is seen rising by 5.9 percent to 10.7 million tonnes, with half of the increase coming from low-cost solvent extraction-electrowon (SX-EW) output.
However, demand has been strong this year, and is expected to register four percent growth, keeping total commercial stocks under five weeks consumption.
But by the end of the year capacity expansions will start to have an impact on stocks, particularly on the LME.
This is likely to induce considerable pressure on the price, although the market will remain vulnerable to supply disruptions as well as the level of Chinese imports, Wolff added.
